Neutrality rearranges the MAINTAINER's repository to serve a contributor who has not arrived yet, which is a harder sell than a language feature. RFC-6 adds a capability a maintainer can evaluate on its merits; RFC-15 asks them to stop tracking .claude/ and make a gate conditional, and the benefit accrues to someone with different tooling rather than to the person reviewing it. The costs measured on this fork are also mostly costs THIS fork pays, because this fork is the one that installed a second harness - a maintainer with one harness sees none of the drift and none of the merge-commit imposition. Only the first cost is unconditional: control-plane-check.py exits 1 on a bare clone for anyone. So the honest framing weakens the ask, and the dishonest one - leading with costs that are really ours - would not survive a maintainer checking them.
